reviewNote: kneecap is pre-release and installs unsigned onto the reader's own phone, so the iPhone build stops working after 7 days until it is rebuilt — the guide says so before the first command. It is an independent community fork of OpenCut (MIT) and is not affiliated with CapCut or ByteDance; no CapCut assets are bundled. Everything runs on-device: no account, no server, no upload.

setupSteps.title: Install Git
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Git responds with a version number

setupSteps.title: Install Node LTS
setupSteps.verifierLabel: Node responds with a version number

steps.title: Open Terminal
steps.body: Keep it open beside Iris.
steps.verifierLabel: Terminal is open

steps.title: Check Git and Node
steps.body: Git and the current Node LTS are required.
steps.verifierLabel: Git and Node respond with version numbers

steps.title: Install Bun
steps.body: kneecap's workspace is built with Bun. This installs it through npm.
steps.verifierLabel: Bun responds with a version number

expect.prompt: In the shell, has `npm install -g bun` finished — a summary line such as "added 1 package" or "changed 1 package", with the prompt back and no error? Answer not done while it is still downloading, or if it stopped on a permissions error such as EACCES.

hints: If npm refused for lack of permission, reinstall Node from nodejs.org rather than re-running this with more privileges.
Finished but still not found? Open a fresh shell window so the new PATH is picked up.

steps.title: Copy kneecap to this Mac
steps.command:
cd ~
if [ ! -d kneecap/.git ]; then
git clone https://github.com/Blueturboguy07/kneecap.git
fi
steps.verifierLabel: A kneecap folder appears

steps.title: Open the kneecap folder
steps.verifierLabel: Your terminal prompt is inside the kneecap folder

steps.title: Use the reviewed version
steps.verifierLabel: Git reports the reviewed commit

steps.title: Install the workspace
steps.body: A few minutes the first time — it is a Rust and TypeScript monorepo.
steps.verifierLabel: The command finishes without an error

steps.title: Build the editor
steps.body: Bundles the editor into apps/mobile/www — the assets the phone app loads offline.
steps.verifierLabel: Vite reports the build finished

expect.prompt: Does the terminal show a finished Vite build — a list of written bundle files and a 'built in' line — with the prompt back and no error?

hints: If it cannot find vite, the workspace install above did not finish — run it again from the kneecap folder.
Errors mentioning opencut-wasm mean the Rust package did not build; re-run the install step before this one.

steps.title: Install Xcode
steps.body: Free, and large — start it now. Open it once and accept the licence.
steps.verifierLabel: Xcode opens to its welcome screen

steps.title: Copy the editor into the iPhone app
steps.verifierLabel: Capacitor reports the sync finished

steps.title: Open the iPhone project
steps.body: Capacitor 8 uses Swift Package Manager, so there is no workspace file to hunt for.
steps.verifierLabel: Xcode opens the App project and finishes resolving packages

steps.title: Sign it with your Apple ID
steps.body: Pick App, then Signing & Capabilities, then add your Apple ID as the Team.
steps.verifierLabel: The signing panel shows your name and no red error

point.descriptor: the Signing & Capabilities tab in the App target editor

steps.title: Plug in your iPhone and press play
steps.body: Pick your iPhone in the device menu, then the play button. First build is slow.
steps.verifierLabel: kneecap appears on your home screen

point.descriptor: the play button at the top left of Xcode's toolbar

steps.title: Trust the app on your iPhone
steps.body: Settings, General, VPN & Device Management, your Apple ID, then Trust.
steps.verifierLabel: kneecap opens instead of showing an Untrusted Developer message

steps.title: Check that it works
steps.body: Open kneecap, start a project, add a clip from your camera roll, then Export.
steps.verifierLabel: The exported video saves back to your camera roll

unsupported.headline: A Windows PC cannot build an iPhone app
unsupported.reason: Apple only allows iPhone apps to be built and signed on macOS using Xcode, which Apple does not release for Windows. This is Apple's restriction, not a missing feature in kneecap — no emulator or virtual machine makes it work reliably.
alternatives: Borrow a Mac for about half an hour — the signature it installs lasts 7 days and can be renewed on any Mac.
Use an Android phone instead, which builds fine from Windows and has its own export pipeline.
Edit on the desktop web build instead — no install, though it has no phone camera roll and no on-device export.
